heroHeadline: RSF Drone Kills 27 at SAF High-Level Meeting in Singa; Drone War Reaches Sennar State on Day 1111
heroSubtitle: An RSF drone strike on April 30 hit a Sudanese Armed Forces military base in Singa (Sennar State capital) during a high-level meeting of commanders and officials, killing at least 27 and wounding 73 — one of the deadliest single RSF drone strikes of the war. Senior officers were among the dead; Sennar State Governor Al-Zubair Hassan Al-Sayed survived. The strike follows the April 29 RSF drone wave on the 18th Infantry Division HQ in Kosti and Kenana airbase (White Nile State), demonstrating RSF's expanding long-range drone reach across SAF-controlled central and eastern Sudan. On the ground, the Sudan Doctors Network reported April 27 that RSF is detaining 2,377 people in El Fasher — including 426 children, 370 women, and 22 doctors — in deplorable conditions with a cholera outbreak that has killed 300 detainees since February. A measles outbreak has killed ~70 and infected ~1,000 in Labado (East Darfur). On Day 1111 of Sudan's civil war, approximately 700 civilians were killed by drone strikes in Q1 2026 alone, and the UN documents 34 million people — 65% of Sudan's population — in urgent need of humanitarian support with only 16% of the $3 billion 2026 appeal funded.
